title: Endomorphism fibres: signed double-cone interchange and augmented triangle maps
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and use integer cochain complexes with $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^q=B^q\oplus A^{q+1}$, differential $(b,a)\mapsto(db+fa,-da)$ and cone boundary $-p$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $s:A\to A$ and $t:B\to B$ be chain endomorphisms, and let $f:A\to B$ be a chain map with $fs=tf$. Put $K(A,s)=\operatorname{Cone}(s)[-1]$, in coordinates $K(A,s)^q=A^q\oplus A^{q-1}$ with differential $(dv,-du-sv)$; define $K(B,t)$ similarly and let $K(f)=\operatorname{diag}(f,f)$. The diagonal map $c=\operatorname{diag}(t,s)$ is a chain endomorphism of $C=\operatorname{Cone}(f)$. There is a chain isomorphism
$$\Phi_f:K(C,c)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(K(f)),\qquad(b,a,b',a')\mapsto(b,b',a,-a'),$$
in source order $B^q,A^{q+1},B^{q-1},A^q$, with inverse $(b,b',a,h)\mapsto(b,a,b',-h)$. It is natural in strictly commuting squares $(\alpha,\beta)$ between such $f$ and $\widetilde f$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ intertwine the respective endomorphisms. If $i:B\to C$ and $-p:C\to A[1]$ are the cone inclusion and boundary, then
$$\Phi_f K(i)=i_{K(f)},\qquad\sigma_1 K(-p)=(-p_{K(f)})\Phi_f,$$
where $\sigma_1:K(A[1],s[1])\to K(A,s)[1]$ is $(v,u)\mapsto(v,-u)$ and $K$ sends an intertwining map to its diagonal map.
Let $g:M\to M'$ be any chain map and let $J:M\to A$, $J':M'\to B$ satisfy $sJ=0$, $tJ'=0$, and $fJ=J'g$. Write $J_C:\operatorname{Cone}(g)\to C$ for the diagonal cone map $(m',m)\mapsto(J'm',Jm)$. The maps $\eta_J=(J,0)$, $\eta_{J'}=(J',0)$ and $\eta_{J_C}=(J_C,0)$ are chain maps to the respective fibres, and
$$\Phi_f\eta_{J_C}=\operatorname{Cone}(\eta_J,\eta_{J'}),$$
where the right side is the cone map induced by the strictly commuting square $K(f)\eta_J=\eta_{J'}g$. No countable-product, boundedness or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Cones paragraph, cone commutation and canonical triangle maps. Coordinate conventions: Stacks Tag 014E (derived.tex, definition-cone), Tag 014Q (derived.tex, definition-distinguished-triangle) and Tag 011G (homology.tex, definition-shift-cochain).

proof.text: Use biproduct component notation throughout: a tuple denotes the matrix of a morphism into a finite biproduct, not an assumption that objects of $\mathcal A$ have elements. Finite biproducts and bilinear composition are available by [def-sp-abelian]. The cone and shift definitions [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] give $K(V,r)^q=V^q\oplus V^{q-1}$ and $d_K(v,u)=(dv,-du-rv)$ after swapping the two summands of $\operatorname{Cone}(r)[-1]$. Its differential squares to zero because its second component is $dr v-rd v=0$, and its first component is $d^2v=0$. For any chain map $a$ with $ar=r'a$, both $d_KK(a)(v,u)$ and $K(a)d_K(v,u)$ are $(a\,dv,-a\,du-r'a v)$. Thus the diagonal maps used below are chain maps. Finally $d_Cc(b,a)=(t\,db+fs a,-s\,da)$ and $cd_C(b,a)=(t\,db+tf a,-s\,da)$; these agree by $fs=tf$. Hence $c$ is a chain endomorphism and both sides of the proposed isomorphism are complexes.

Explicit component computation for the Cones paragraph of literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction.proof.md

proof.text:
Expand the two differentials using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In the stated source order, the differential of $K(C,c)$ is
$$D_S(b,a,b',a')=(db+fa,-da,-db'-fa'-tb,da'-sa).$$
In target order $B^q,B^{q-1},A^{q+1},A^q$, the differential of $\operatorname{Cone}(K(f))$ is
$$D_T(b,b',a,h)=(db+fa,-db'-tb+fh,-da,dh+sa).$$
Define $\Phi_f^q(b,a,b',a')=(b,b',a,-a')$ by the indicated signed biproduct permutation [def-sp-abelian]. Substitution gives
$$D_T\Phi_f(b,a,b',a')=(db+fa,-db'-tb-fa',-da,-da'+sa)=\Phi_fD_S(b,a,b',a').$$
Thus the prescribed degree maps form a chain map. All equations are identities of the four component morphisms.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone; Tag 014Q, definition-distinguished-triangle (the following paragraph specifies the boundary -p). Explicit component computation for the Cones paragraph of literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction.proof.md

proof.text: Let $\Psi_f^q(b,b',a,h)=(b,a,b',-h)$. By the biproduct identities [def-sp-abelian], both $\Psi_f^q\Phi_f^q$ and $\Phi_f^q\Psi_f^q$ are identities. The chain identity from step 2 implies $D_S\Psi_f=\Psi_fD_T$ by multiplying $D_T\Phi_f=\Phi_fD_S$ on the left and right by these degreewise inverses. Therefore $\Psi_f$ is a chain inverse. For a square $\beta f=\widetilde f\alpha$ with $\alpha s=\widetilde s\alpha$ and $\beta t=\widetilde t\beta$, the induced source map is $(b,a,b',a')\mapsto(\beta b,\alpha a,\beta b',\alpha a')$, and the induced target map is $(b,b',a,h)\mapsto(\beta b,\beta b',\alpha a,\alpha h)$. The square commutes since both composites send $(b,a,b',a')$ to $(\beta b,\beta b',\alpha a,-\alpha a')$. These diagonal cone maps are chain maps by the cone differential [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the three displayed commutation hypotheses. This proves the asserted naturality.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone; Tag 014Q, definition-distinguished-triangle (the following paragraph specifies the boundary -p). Explicit component computation for the Cones paragraph of literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction.proof.md

proof.text: The shift definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives the differential of $K(A[1],s[1])$ as $(v,u)\mapsto(-dv,du-sv)$. For $\sigma_1(v,u)=(v,-u)$, both $d_{K(A,s)[1]}\sigma_1(v,u)$ and $\sigma_1d_{K(A[1],s[1])}(v,u)$ are $(-dv,-du+sv)$. This is a chain isomorphism with inverse the same signed formula, by [def-sp-abelian]. The inclusion $i$ intertwines $t,c$, while $-p$ intertwines $c,s[1]$ because $ci=it$ and $(-p)c=s[1](-p)$. Consequently their fibre maps are the diagonal chain maps from step 1. On $(b,b')$, both $\Phi_fK(i)$ and $i_{K(f)}$ are $(b,b',0,0)$. On $(b,a,b',a')$, the map $K(-p)$ gives $(-a,-a')$, and applying $\sigma_1$ gives $(-a,a')$. Applying $\Phi_f$ and then the boundary $-p_{K(f)}$ also gives $(-a,a')$. This proves both triangle identities with the specified negative cone boundaries.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain; together with Stacks Tag 014E, derived.tex, definition-cone. Explicit component computation for the Cones paragraph of literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction.proof.md

proof.text:
The given $J,J'$ are morphisms of complexes, and $sJ=0$, $tJ'=0$. For each pair $(V,r)$ and chain map $L:M\to V$ with $rL=0$, the fibre differential gives $d_K(Lm,0)=(L\,dm,-rLm)=(L\,dm,0)$. Hence $\eta_J$ and $\eta_{J'}$ are chain maps. The identity $fJ=J'g$ gives $K(f)\eta_J(m)=(fJm,0)=(J'gm,0)=\eta_{J'}g(m)$, as an identity of biproduct components [def-sp-abelian]. The cone differential [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives
$$d_CJ_C(m',m)=(J'\,dm'+fJm,-J\,dm)=(J'(dm'+gm),-J\,dm)=J_Cd_{\operatorname{Cone}(g)}(m',m).$$
Thus $J_C$ is a chain map. Also $cJ_C=(tJ',sJ)=0$, so the same fibre calculation proves that $\eta_{J_C}$ is a chain map.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone; Tag 014Q, definition-distinguished-triangle (the following paragraph specifies the boundary -p). Explicit component computation for the Cones paragraph of literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama/sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction.proof.md

proof.text: For the strictly commuting square in step 5, define its cone map by the diagonal formula $(m',m)\mapsto(\eta_{J'}m',\eta_Jm)$. It is a chain map: its differential is $(\eta_{J'}dm'+K(f)\eta_Jm,-\eta_Jdm)=(\eta_{J'}(dm'+gm),-\eta_Jdm)$ by step 5, which is the diagonal formula after the source cone differential [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Now $\eta_{J_C}(m',m)$ has source coordinates $(J'm',Jm,0,0)$, so $\Phi_f\eta_{J_C}(m',m)=(J'm',0,Jm,0)$. These are exactly the target coordinates of $\operatorname{Cone}(\eta_J,\eta_{J'})(m',m)$. Equality holds by the biproduct component identities [def-sp-abelian]. All constructions and checks are degreewise finite biproduct calculations; they make no assumption about countable products, boundedness, or epimorphisms.
